source: X Help Center - Rules and Policies

category.name: Safety and cybercrime
category.description: Policies that enforce our principles against abuse, harassment, violence and criminal actions on the >x< platform.

policies.title: Abuse and harassment
policies.summary: You may not target others with abuse or harassment, or encourage other people to do so.

targeted_harassment: Sharing multiple Posts over a short period of time, or continuously posting replies with malicious content to target an individual (including dedicated harassment accounts)
Mentioning or tagging users with malicious content
violations.violent_event_denial: Content denying verified mass murder or mass casualty events (e.g., Holocaust, school shootings, terrorist attacks, natural disasters) when shared with abusive context, such as calling them a 'hoax' or claiming victims are 'actors'.
violations.incitement_of_harassment: Encouraging others to harass or target specific individuals or groups, online or offline.
unwanted_sexual_content_and_graphic_obje: Sending unsolicited and/or unwanted adult media (images, videos, GIFs)
Unwanted sexual discussion of someone's body
Any content that sexualizes an individual without their consent
violations.insults: Action is taken against insults or profanity used to target others, but not every instance of insulting terms.
violations.use_of_prior_names_and_pronouns: Where required by local laws, visibility of posts purposefully using wrong pronouns or a previous name (deadnaming) is reduced; requires first-person confirmation from the target.

not_violations: Consensual use of terms between friends in a clearly non-abusive context
Calling attention to, condemning, or highlighting others' harmful behaviors
Criticism of institutions, practices and ideas
policies.reporting: Anyone can report via the dedicated reporting flow; sometimes the target must be heard first.
enforcement: Reducing visibility (removal from search, recommendations, trends, notifications, timelines; restricting discoverability; downranking; limiting engagement; excluding adjacent ads)
Excluding posts/accounts from email or in-product recommendations
Requiring post removal (possible read-only mode; subsequent violations may lead to suspension)
Suspending accounts dedicated to Unwanted Sexual Content & Graphic Objectification or to harassing individuals

policies.title: Abusive profile information
policies.summary: You may not use your username, display name, or profile bio to engage in abusive behavior, such as targeted harassment or expressing hate towards a person, group, or protected category.
policies.rationale: Accounts with abusive profile information usually indicate abusive intent and strongly correlate with abusive behavior. High visibility of profile names/descriptions may expose people to threatening or abusive content.
violations: Abusive slurs, epithets, racist or sexist tropes
Abusive content that reduces someone to less than human
not_violations: Insults (but other policies may still apply if posts/DMs violate them)
notes: Both first-person and bystander reports are reviewed
Context matters when evaluating abusive behavior
enforcement: Permanent suspension on first violation for abusive profile information
Hateful symbols must be removed before the account can be used again; repeated violations lead to permanent suspension
Appeal available if suspended in error

policies.title: Adult Content Policy
policies.summary: You may share consensually produced and distributed adult nudity or sexual behavior, provided it's properly labeled and not prominently displayed.
policies.definition: Any consensually produced and distributed material depicting adult nudity or sexual behavior that is pornographic or intended to cause sexual arousal, including AI-generated, photographic or animated content (cartoons, hentai, anime). Examples: full/partial nudity (close-ups of genitals, buttocks, breasts); explicit or implied sexual behavior or simulated acts.

adult_nudity: Visible genitals or anus exposed, focused on, or prominently featured
sexual_behavior: Explicit sexual activity including vaginal, oral or anal sex, sex toys, or any form of sexual penetration
Implied sexual activity including clothed sexual simulation, states of arousal (erection), or pixelated/blurred/strategically covered sexual activity
Bodily fluids in a sexual context

allowed_without_label: Medical content (e.g., post-surgery media of breast augmentation or mastectomy)
Partial or digitally obscured nudity (modeling or beach photos)
Activist campaigns carried out with nudity
Artistic nudity or sexual behavior (paintings, drawings, sculptures, statues)
Parody or satire conveying political ideas (caricatures, cartoons)
Humor/memes with no intent to cause sexual arousal
not_allowed: Adult Content in highly visible areas: live video, profile pictures, headers, List banners, Community cover photos

Content violating other rules: non-consensual nudity, promoting/soliciting sexual services, child sexual exploitation, violent sexual conduct, unwanted sexual content & graphic objectification, bestiality and necrophilia
marking_content: Regular posters should adjust media settings so all images/videos are behind a content warning
One-time content warnings can be added per post
X will adjust account settings if posts are repeatedly unmarked
Users under 18 (or without a birth date on profile) cannot view marked content
policies.enforcement: Removal from highly visible areas; subsequent violations may result in read-only mode or suspension.
policies.reporting: Anyone can report unmarked content via the in-app reporting flow.
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if a mistake was made.

policies.title: Child Safety Policy
policies.summary: Zero tolerance for any forms of child sexual exploitation; certain media depicting physical child abuse is removed to prevent normalization of violence against children. 'Children/minors' = any person under 18.

child_sexual_exploitation.scope: Real, text, illustrated, or computer-generated media (including generative AI). Viewing, sharing, linking, or engaging contributes to re-victimization.
not_allowed: Depictions of a child in sexually explicit or suggestive acts (including edits like obscuring faces/body parts)
Sexualized commentaries about or directed at a known or unknown minor
Links to third-party sites hosting child sexual exploitation materials
Fantasies about or promoting child sexual exploitation
Identifying alleged victims by name or image
Promoting or normalizing sexual attraction to minors as identity/orientation
Sending sexually explicit media to a child or engaging a child in sexual conversation
Obtaining sexual media from a child or engaging a child in sexual activity via blackmail/incentives
Recruiting, advertising, or expressing interest in commercial sex acts involving a child, or harboring/transporting a child for sexual purposes
Threatening to share or requesting sexual media of minors, including self-generated media, especially via blackmail/bounty tactics
allowed_exceptions_low_risk: Discussion that does not promote/glorify CSE or identify potential victims
Victims sharing their stories without explicit details or media
Help-seeking conversations for those struggling with attraction to minors
Advocacy against illegal/harmful activity involving minors without sharing/linking CSE material
enforcement: Immediate and permanent suspension in the majority of cases
Reports to NCMEC for content depicting/promoting CSE, including third-party links
Some violations may only require post removal; subsequent violations may lead to suspension

assessment_criteria: Whether the child is nude, partially clothed, or fully clothed
Severity of harm the child is experiencing
not_allowed: Media where the child is nude and experiencing any type of harm
Media shared with abusive context
Media where the child is experiencing moderate or major harm
physical_child_abuse_media.restricted_reach: Limited exceptions (identifying a child to rescue them or identify the perpetrator; news organizations) — must be placed behind the Graphic Content warning.
enforcement: Content warning or post removal (possible read-only mode; subsequent violations may lead to suspension)
Suspension of accounts whose sole purpose is such behavior

assessment_criteria: Report from the minor or authorized representative
media_of_minors_in_physical_altercation.restricted_reach: Limited exceptions (e.g., news organizations); may require a content warning.
enforcement: Post removal upon report (possible read-only mode; subsequent violations may lead to suspension)
Abusive Behavior policies may apply for abusive content toward the victim
Sensitive Media policies may apply for graphic content/gratuitous gore

policies.reporting: Anyone can report via in-app flow or the Help Center form (no X account needed). Contact local law enforcement if a child is at immediate risk. NCMEC CyberTipline: report.cybertip.org / 1-800-843-5678.
policies.important_note: Engaging with CSE content can be illegal. Report immediately; do not like, reply, quote-post, screenshot, or follow distributing accounts. No evidence needed in the report.
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if a mistake was made.

policies.title: Hateful Conduct
policies.summary: You may not directly attack other people on the basis of race, ethnicity, national origin, caste, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, religious affiliation, age, disability, or serious disease.

violations.hateful_references: Content referencing violence or violent events where a protected category was the primary target/victims, with intent to harass (e.g., genocides like the Holocaust, lynchings).
incitement: Inciting fear or spreading fearful stereotypes about a protected category
Inciting others to harass members of a protected category on or off platform
Inciting discrimination via denial of economic support based on protected category (political commentary, boycotts, and protests excluded)
violations.slurs_and_tropes: Repeated slurs, tropes, or content degrading/reinforcing harmful stereotypes. Severe/repetitive use may require Post removal; moderate/isolated use may limit visibility.
violations.dehumanization: Dehumanizing a group based on religion, caste, age, disability, serious disease, national origin, race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, or sexual orientation.
violations.hateful_imagery: Logos, symbols, or images promoting hostility/malice (e.g., Nazi swastika; images depicting others as less than human; images altered with hateful symbols or mass murder references). Not permitted in live video, account bio, profile or header images; elsewhere must be marked sensitive. Unsolicited sending is also a violation.
violations.hateful_profile: No hateful images/symbols in profile image or header; no abusive username, display name, or bio.

notes: First-person and bystander reports reviewed; context is verified with the target when needed
No need to prove membership in a protected category; X never investigates this
enforcement: Reducing visibility (removal from search/recommendations/trends/notifications/timelines, restricting discoverability, downranking, limiting engagement, excluding adjacent ads)
Excluding posts/accounts from email or in-product recommendations
Requiring post removal (possible read-only mode)
Suspending accounts violating the Hateful Profile policy
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if suspended in error.

policies.title: Non-consensual Intimate Content Policy
policies.summary: You may not share, create, manipulate, distribute or threaten to distribute content that sexualizes or exposes an identifiable real adult without their explicit consent (sometimes called 'revenge porn').

covered: Creation or capture of non-consensual media
Manipulation or edits, including AI or any other tool
Sharing or threatening distribution, including screenshots of private conversations
Bounties, incentives, or instructions for unauthorized access (even without media attached)
violations.formats: Real photographs, videos, GIFs, AI-generated or edited media, screenshots, third-party links or previews.
examples: Hidden camera, creepshot, or upskirt content featuring nudity or sexual acts
Non-consensual explicit nudity or sexual activity (including implied acts or fetish content)
Bodily fluids in a sexual context without explicit consent
AI-generated, deepfake, or digitally manipulated media sexualizing a specific individual
Intimate/private-setting media (bedroom, bathroom, dressing room) not intended for public distribution
Prompting, attempting to generate, generating, or sharing non-consensual intimate AI content of real people (even if unsuccessful)

not_violations: Content with clear signals of explicit consent (person posting it themselves with affirmative language; depicted individual replying with approval)
Images/videos in public or commercial settings, streams, conventions, performances, voluntary on-camera appearances
Widely circulated public/media-published photos of public figures/celebrities
Political satire, memes, humor, or non-sexual edits critical of public figures
Consensual adult nudity or sexual acts marked as Adult Content
policies.minors_note: Any depiction, generation, or sexualization of a minor (under 18) is treated as highest-severity and routed to the dedicated Child Safety team.

reporting.desktop: Use the private information report form and select the relevant option.

enforcement: Suspension for original posters of non-consensual intimate media, and accounts dedicated to this content; reshares/quotes/reposts also violate
First-time inadvertent/shock-awareness sharing: content removal, temporary account lock; repeat violation = permanent suspension
If consent is unclear (non-explicit), visibility limited until the victim is heard
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if a mistake was made.

policies.title: Perpetrators of violent attacks policy
policies.summary: Accounts maintained by individual perpetrators of terrorist, violent extremist, or mass violent attacks — and accounts glorifying perpetrators or sharing manifestos — are removed. Posts disseminating manifestos may also be removed.
policies.manifesto_definition: A statement by a perpetrator outlining motivation, views, or intent to engage in a violent attack (written document, social media post, audio, video, link, letter). May be shared before or after the attack; linked via statement of warning or intent.
policies.scope_note: Attacks claimed by violent organizations fall under the Violent and Hateful Entities policy; no confirmed group affiliation is required for enforcement here.
violations: Sharing or linking full-length manifestos regardless of context

Posts with manifesto excerpts except in newsworthy context (always prohibited: excerpts on arming oneself/choosing targets; hateful slogans, symbols, memes, hateful conspiracy theories like the Great Replacement Theory; perpetrator's ideology, tactical choices, or plan of attack)
Perpetrator-generated media related to the attack (media filmed by perpetrator, memes/stickers/graffiti, media of weapons used)
Bystander content of the attack in progress (assault/death moments, dead bodies, identifying victims, depicting the perpetrator conducting the attack)
multimedia_urls_hashtags: Sensitive media interstitials for media depicting perpetrators and newsworthy manifesto excerpts
Denylisting hashtags identifying perpetrators or used to surface manifestos
not_violations: Accounts of bystanders who stopped the attack (e.g., shot the perpetrator)
Accounts of perpetrators whose convictions were overturned (not guilty verdict)

Force by law enforcement/military within official functions; violence against military/law enforcement; human rights abuses; armed conflict; self-defense; probable doubt about intent; vandalism of essential infrastructure
Sharing a few sentences from a manifesto in a newsworthy context or to raise awareness (e.g., 'the shooter said he wants to eradicate x group')
policies.reporting: Anyone can report, with or without an X account.
enforcement: Permanent suspension of perpetrator accounts
Removal of manifestos and perpetrator/accomplice content
Removal also applies under Violent Speech and other Rules

policies.title: Private information policy
policies.summary: You may not threaten to expose, incentivize others to expose, or publish other people's private information without express authorization, or share private media of individuals without their consent ('doxxing').
assessment_factors: Type of information (physical location and phone numbers are higher risk)
Who is sharing it and whether they have consent
Whether the information is already publicly available elsewhere (home addresses may still be actioned)
Intent of the person sharing (abusive/harassing intent → action; crisis help → may not action)
posting_private_information_violations: Home address or physical location info (street addresses, GPS coordinates, private location identifiers)
Identity documents (government IDs, social security/national identity numbers)
Contact info (non-public phone numbers, emails, passwords)
Health-related private information (biometric data, medical records)
Identity of an anonymous user (name or media depicting them)
Threatening to publicly expose private information
Sharing info enabling hacking/unauthorized access (e.g., banking login credentials)
Asking for/offering bounties in exchange for posting private information
Asking for bounties in exchange for NOT posting (blackmail)
policies.right_to_privacy: Cannot share media (photos/videos) of private individuals without the permission of the person(s) depicted. Not applicable to public figures.

posting_private_information: People sharing their own private information
Identity documents/numbers from regions where they're not considered private

Not considered private: names, birthdates/ages, education/employment places, publicly available business locations, physical appearance descriptions, gossip/rumors/accusations/allegations, screenshots of messages (unless containing private info)
right_to_privacy: Media adding value to public discourse or shared in public interest
Eyewitness accounts/on-the-ground reports from developing events

reporting.posting_private_information: Anyone can report via the dedicated flow when clearly abusive; otherwise owner (or authorized representative) may need to report.
reporting.right_to_privacy: First-person reports required: from the depicted individual or an authorized representative (parents/legal guardians, lawyers, legal representatives).

enforcement: Requiring post removal (possible read-only mode; subsequent violations may lead to suspension)
Suspending accounts solely dedicated to posting others' private information/media (including upskirt/creepshot accounts)
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if enforced in error.

policies.title: Suicide and Self-harm Policy
policies.summary: You may share content seeking support, discussing recovery, or raising awareness — but content that encourages, promotes, actively engages in, or depicts self-harm behaviors is against the Rules.

self_harm_behaviors: Self-inflicted physical harm (cutting, burning, scratching, re-opening wounds, inserting needles)
Harmful drug use or substance abuse

not_allowed: Encouraging someone to physically harm or kill themselves
Asking others for encouragement to self-harm, including seeking partners for group suicides or suicide games
Sharing information, strategies, methods, or instructions assisting self-harm and suicide
Suggesting wounds or self-harm methods are insufficiently severe
Describing self-harm as healthy coping or sophisticated/artistic response
Content discouraging recovery or help seeking
Media depicting self-harm behaviors without recovery context
policies.predatory_behavior: Content or accounts exhibiting predatory behavior targeting children (especially exhibiting self-harm behaviors) is not allowed; minors' accounts may be suspended protectively if interacting with known predators.
policies.high_visibility: Not allowed in live video, profile pictures, headers, List banners, or Community cover photos; removal required, subsequent violations may lead to read-only mode or suspension.
allowed_with_support: Personal disclosures about ongoing/past self-harm, suicidal ideation, emotional distress, or recovery
Media of scars with recovery context (not graphic, e.g., healed scars)
Research, advocacy, and education discussions on self-harm/suicide prevention
policies.note: People can share personal experiences but should avoid detailed strategies/methods to prevent inadvertently encouraging self-harm.
policies.crisis_support: On reports of self-harm/suicide intent, X contacts the person, encourages support, provides hotline resources; may work with law enforcement (e.g., valid emergency disclosure requests).
policies.reporting: Anyone can report via in-app flow or the specialized reporting form; reports go to a dedicated team.
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if a mistake was made.

policies.title: Violent and hateful entities policy
policies.summary: You may not threaten terrorism and/or violent extremism, nor promote violent and hateful entities.

definitions.violent_entities: Entities that deliberately target humans or essential infrastructure with physical violence and/or violent rhetoric to further their cause (terrorist organizations, violent extremist groups, perpetrators of violent attacks).
definitions.hateful_entities: Entities that have systematically and intentionally promoted, supported, and/or advocated for hateful conduct, including violence or targeted harassment towards a protected category.

violations: Engaging in or promoting violent acts on behalf of, or directly/indirectly for, a violent or hateful entity
Recruiting, or providing/distributing services (media/propaganda) to further stated goals
exceptions: Entities that have reformed or denounced their violence/hate-based purpose
Entities currently engaged in a peaceful resolution process
State or governmental entities, including those with elected representatives
policies.not_violations: Educational, documentary, and/or newsworthy discussion of violent and hateful entities.

reporting.who: Anyone, with or without an X account

policies.enforcement: Immediate and permanent suspension of any violating account. Appeal available if suspended in error.

policies.title: Violent Content Policy
policies.summary: You may share graphic media if properly labeled, not prominently displayed, and not excessively gory or depicting sexual violence — but explicitly threatening, inciting, glorifying, or expressing desire for violence is not allowed.

violent_speech.definition: Content that threatens, incites, glorifies, or expresses desire for violence or harm.
not_allowed: Violent Threats: threatening to kill, torture, sexually assault, or otherwise hurt someone; threatening damage to civilian homes/shelters or essential infrastructure
Wish of Harm: hoping others die, suffer illnesses, tragic incidents, or other harmful consequences
Incitement of Violence: inciting/promoting/encouraging violence, self-harm, or atrocity crimes (crimes against humanity, war crimes, genocide)
Glorification of Violence: glorifying/praising/celebrating acts of violence, including by Violent Entities; glorifying animal abuse or cruelty
violent_speech.high_visibility_restriction: Not allowed in live video, profile, header, bio, list banners, or community cover photos.
restricted_reach_criteria: Context is self-defense or military conflict
Context is outrage/reaction against perpetrators of major harm
Coded language ('dog whistles') indirectly inciting violence
allowed: Hyperbolic/consensual speech between friends or about video games and sporting events
Figures of speech, satire, or artistic expression not instigating actionable violence
Quotes from books/movies, music lyrics, or poetry not instigating actionable violence

violent_media.definition: Visual material depicting graphic, violent, or excessively gory content including sexual violence.
not_allowed: Violent Sexual Conduct: violence (real or simulated) with sexual acts, rape, non-consensual sexual acts, sexualized violence in intimate settings where consent is unclear
Gratuitous Gore: excessively graphic/gruesome content (dismembered/mutilated humans, charred remains, exposed organs/bones, animal torture/killing)
Moment of Death: removal on request from family/authorized representative of images/videos taken at, immediately before, or after an identifiable individual's death
Bestiality & Necrophilia: sexual acts between human and animal, or living human and corpse
violent_media.high_visibility_restriction: Not allowed in highly visible areas or targeting someone nonconsensually with unwanted Violent Media.
restricted_reach_must_be_labeled: Bodily fluids including blood, feces, etc.
Serious physical harm, including visible wounds
Death/violence/medical procedures/serious injury in graphic detail but not excessively gory
Excessively gory media associated with newsworthy events, awareness, or political action, if properly labeled
violent_media.public_interest_note: Public interest factors considered for media depicting deceased individuals; in limited cases media may not be removed despite a valid report.
allowed: Animal violence from hunting/fishing, food manufacturing/processing, bullfighting, or religious sacrifice (unless excessively gory)
Painted or illustrated art portraying violence
Recovery/medical content (scars, healed wounds, stitches, prosthetics)
Simulated blood for events, protests, entertainment, or art
Explosions, altercations, property destruction, surveillance media, or shootings without prohibited Violent Media

marking_content: Regular posters should adjust media settings (content warning behind all images/videos)
One-time content warnings can be added per post
X will adjust account settings if posts are repeatedly unmarked
Users under 18 (or without a birth date) cannot view marked content
reporting: Moment of Death content: family/legal representatives via the Moment of Death report form
Deactivation of deceased person's account: family/estate representatives via the Deactivation report form
All other violations: dedicated in-app reporting flow
policies.appeals: Submit an appeal if a mistake was made.
